It's a real PNG, 782×458, written today at 09:21 — consistent with a clipboard paste into pi. Let me look at it so you know exactly what got pasted.

Nothing sinister — it's pi's own clipboard scratch file.

**What it is:** when you paste an image into the pi TUI, pi dumps the clipboard bitmap to `$TMPDIR/pi-clipboard-<uuid>.png` so it can attach it to the conversation. Your `$TMPDIR` on macOS is that `/var/folders/rr/2ypk...gn/T/` path — a per-user, per-boot temp dir the OS hands out, which is why it looks cryptic.

**What's in this one:** a 782×458 screenshot of a chat app — purple background, a pixel-art blue robot mascot with a `>_` terminal face, and a message input box containing the word "tea" with a blue send arrow. Looks like a screenshot of a Claude/agent-style mobile or web chat UI.

**Is it safe:** yes. `-rw-r--r-- mm staff`, owned by you, written 09:21 today, valid PNG per `file`. macOS clears `/var/folders/.../T/` periodically, and you can delete it now if you want:

```
rm /var/folders/rr/2ypk50n14tq8902_21mkbc840000gn/T/pi-clipboard-*.png
```

The only real consideration is privacy, not security: anything you paste as an image sits in plaintext in temp until the OS reaps it, so avoid pasting screenshots with secrets in them.

**The app writing the file is pi itself** — specifically the session you're talking to me in.

```
69177  pi   ← started 09:21:36, cwd /Users/mm/dev/home-infra  (this session)
11588  pi   ← started yesterday 11:16, same cwd
  └─ 69068 -fish
      └─ 16431 /opt/homebrew/bin/herdr
          └─ 1 launchd
```

Both `pi` processes are children of fish shells under `herdr`. No other process holds the file (`lsof` returned nothing — pi writes it, closes it, and leaves it behind). It's created the instant an image is pasted into the TUI, which is why a new one appeared at 09:26 right after you asked about it.

**On the image itself:** same UI as before, now 373×160 and cropped tighter — the pixel-art blue robot with a `>_` terminal face, and the input pill now reads `teatea` with a red squiggly spell-check underline and a visible text cursor. So these are successive screenshots of the same window, taken while someone types into it.

I still can't name the app with confidence. There's no logo, title bar, URL, or window chrome in frame — just the mascot and the composer. The `>_`-faced robot is terminal/coding-agent branding, and given `herdr` is the thing hosting your pi sessions, a pi-family client is the obvious guess, but that's inference from the mascot, not identification.

Two ways to settle it:
- Take a screenshot with the window chrome/title bar included and paste that.
- Or tell me which window you're screenshotting and I'll check what's running behind it (`lsof`/`ps` on the GUI app).

And if you just want the litter gone rather than explained:

```
rm -f "$TMPDIR"/pi-clipboard-*.png
```

Note that deletes the paste you just made too, so grab anything you still need from it first.
